answer: Bind every agent identity to one hardware secure enclave. At registration the enclave signs a fresh challenge, proving real silicon backs the account, and each chip can sponsor only one identity, so a clone army needs a chip per puppet. One thread of trust runs from chip to ledger: each epoch it re-signs a nonce, and a whisper of doubt — a reused key or a missing signature — freezes earnings until peers re-check. Faking 1,000 agents means buying 1,000 chips at roughly $40 each, about $40,000, while one honest agent pays nothing — like an ocean that admits only one boat per anchor.
